direction: D3: executable skills for SpreadsheetBench and ALFWorld. The explorer claims that a GLM-written ALFWorld state tracker, verified by replay, raises training success well above control, and that SpreadsheetBench programs show little value. My corrected verdict: the numbers are right, but the tracker gain holds only in a solver loop that was redesigned after the tracker failed in the frozen loop. The effect is mixed up with an extra text instruction. The 'learned' program was transcribed from a detailed spec. The comparison against the good instruction was never run, and there is no transfer target.
refuted_claims:
1. "Both arms used max_tokens 512 and the same robust parser; the only difference was the tracker view field."
- Checked: pilot_alf_b.py (md5 e87542c5…, the copy that ran) and pilot_alf_glm.py.
- Found: arm T also adds TRACKER_SENTENCE, which ends "Use it to avoid revisiting places you have already checked." That is a behavioural text instruction. No arm has the sentence alone, so the gain cannot be credited to the program.

2. "Raises training success well above control", with the parser treated as hygiene ("actuator… effect is unmeasured; it could also be a fixed harness fix").
- Recomputed over all 42 paired games: how often the executed action differed from what the frozen loop would have executed (a canonicalised wrapper or the earliest admissible command).
  - T-glm 467/1,139 steps (41.0%); T-hand 438/1,115 (39.3%); C 193/1,462 (13.2%).
  - The most common form was "action: go to X".
  - 25/26 T-glm passes and 27/28 T-hand passes used at least one rescued step; C 11/16.
- Under the frozen verbatim parsing (round-1 pilot; the remote script has no normaliser), 4 of 7 tracker episodes failed with 43 to 50 of 50 actions in wrapper form ('action<|>go to shelf 1<|>', answered by "Nothing happens").
  - The same 7 games in v3 E-ds had 1 wrapper action in 14 runs and passed 7/14; the tracker passed 3/7.
  - train:0004 went from pass/pass to a fail with 50/50 invalid actions.
- Design A (the frozen 32k token cap): 2 of the 3 logged tracker episodes died of runaway truncated replies.
- So the tracker hurt in the frozen loop. The positive effect exists only in a loop redesigned after those failures. Parser and token cap are preconditions that interact with the tracker, not neutral hygiene.

3. The 'learned tracker', framed as 'filled from failure evidence'.
- lt/prompt.json dictates the interface, the EXACT four keys and their meanings, the name format, the observation formats and the statistics behind the goal. GLM transcribed a spec; that explains the 97.7% agreement.
- The design's slot ('view() returning a dict ≤1,500 chars') is far less specified than this prompt, so the pilot does not test induction from failures.
- It is one sample.

4. The 39-game figures are superseded; the run finished at 05:38.
- T-glm 26/42 vs C 16/42: 11 vs 1, p=0.0063, +0.238 [0.092, 0.385].
- T-glm vs T-hand: 26 vs 28, 3 vs 5, p=0.73.
- Tokens per episode 33.3k vs 30.4k; tokens per call 1,225 vs 873.
- Spend was 1,397,767 deepseek tokens, not '~1.21M + ≤0.1M'.

5. "The 5-step window is the mechanism" ('it cannot remember which cabinets it searched').
- In failing episodes, revisits to a receptacle visited within the last 5 steps (so visible to the model): 444/1,017 (44%) E-ds, 418/1,014 (41%) I-ds, 271/504 (54%) pilot-B C.
- About half of the looping is a policy failure that a text rule, or the 'avoid revisiting' sentence, could target.

6. The Chinese verdict's cost, "约1400万词元、约8小时" (about 14M tokens, about 8 hours), covers only the empty-scaffold half.
- The English recommendation adds a repetition with the task-card Skill. v3 I-ds cost 3,377 tokens per call and 105.7k per episode (12,044,182/114).
- 456 task-card episodes ≈ 45 to 50M tokens and another 8 to 12 h. Total ≈ 60 to 65M tokens and 16 to 24 h.
- The omitted half is exactly the good-instruction comparison.

7. "SpreadsheetBench programs show little value."
- Only check + one repair was piloted: R 14/47 vs S 11/47, 8 vs 5, p=0.58. That is inconclusive, not negative.
- The library slot was never piloted.
- The hard-check precision (290/780 fails flagged, 0/599 passes) is mostly trivial: 213/290 flags are 'no_workbook', which the harness already records. Semantic flags cover 84/780.
- Liu et al. 2026, which the explorer cites, has evolved skills 30.96 points ABOVE oracle parallel sampling on SpreadsheetBench. The report does not reconcile this.

8. "纯属偶然的可能性约千分之四" (a chance of about 0.4% that this is pure luck) misreads p=0.0042.

9. Minor: SpreadsheetBench multi-round inference beats single-round for most models, but GPT-4o declined in the main table (18.35 to 16.96).
confirmed_claims:
Harness:
- ALFWorld view: initial observation, current observation, admissible commands, recent_history[-5:] (backends.py:744-746). The action is executed verbatim; the Skill is re-sent every step; 50 steps.
- SpreadsheetBench: one call per cell; preview of 5 rows x 20 columns.
- Manifest runtime: image sha256:0a0a5dcb…, 300 s, 4,096 MB, 1 CPU, contract-first-v2, explicit-python-fences-v1, qualified_lo_recalc_v7_v1.
- The training pool is historical train + val (data.py pool(); ALFWorld 39+18). The alfworld/val:* games are training items.
- Identity sites: cells.py:222, evaluation.py:356/366 (reuse keyed on the text digest), step.py:825, chain.py:290.

v3 s5/train recount:
- Passes: E-ds 46/114, I-ds 58/114. All failures used the full 50 steps (68/68, 56/56).
- Repeated go-to per failing episode: 15.0 and 18.1 (explorer: 14.9 and 17.8).
- On the 42 pilot games: 30/84 and 38/84; 6 of 42 games flip between runs.
- Training replies max out at 202 and 20 completion tokens, none above 512. So the 106 replies above 512 and the 32,768 maximum come from gate cells.

Pilot B:
- 28/42 vs 16/42, 14 vs 2, p=0.0042, +0.286 [0.118, 0.453].
- The 42 games are the first 42 in hash order before the budget stop, not chosen by outcome.

Learned tracker and replay:
- Hashes ed49e788… and 1c6c4da0… match.
- Replay: 0 exceptions; agreement on 7,350/7,524 steps; 0 property failures. GLM call used 4,986 tokens.
- tracker_glm.py uses only the standard library and contains no game-specific literals.

SpreadsheetBench:
- Repair vs re-sample p=0.581. Salvage of 91 unclosed fences: 31 pass, 58 fail, 2 unknown.
- Code shares match: D4 52/87; D1+D2+D5+D6 25/87.

Literature checked:
- Voyager: 3.3x more unique items, milestones up to 15.3x faster.
- AdaPlanner: 91.79% on 134 tasks with text-davinci-002.
- ASI: +23.5% / +11.3% (COLM 2025 per the paper header).
- SkillWeaver: 31.8% / 39.8%.
- StateAct: more than 10% over ReAct on ALFWorld (REALM 2025).
- SpreadsheetBench: NeurIPS 2024 D&B.
- Liu et al. 2026: 55/388 and 30.96 points, with the evolved skill higher.

Hard rules: no violation found. The earlier globs s[45]/*/attempt-* cannot reach s*/evaluation/<bench>/attempt-* (chain.py:138), and the detector keeps only the train, selftest, screen and confirm units.
notes_cn: 核对：数字基本属实。最终42局：分析模型GLM写的记事工具成功26局，对照16局（11局变好、1局变差），与手写版28局无差别。但有四个问题：一、提升依赖改过的评测程序：带工具时约41%的步骤动作格式写错，靠新加的自动纠正才能执行，对照组只有13%；在接近原样的两次试玩里，带工具的10局有6局因格式错或回复过长而失败。二、实验组多了一句“避免重复去查过的地方”的文字指令，没单独对照。三、给GLM的提示已写明要记哪四项，是照规格写代码，不算从经验学到。四、没和“好的任务说明”比，也没有相似考试测迁移；加上任务说明的复现约需4500万到5000万词元（模型计费单位），中文结论写的1400万偏低。
